title: ReSMiPS: A ReRAM-based Sparse Mixed-precision Solver with Fast Matrix Reordering Algorithm
problem: Sparse matrix equation solvers on digital platforms suffer from memory bandwidth bottlenecks in large-scale storage and computation; ReRAM-based CIM offers promise but struggles to achieve high precision and energy efficiency simultaneously.
method: ReSMiPS combines a novel Fast Sparse Matrix Reordering (FSMR) algorithm with an In-memory float64 (IF64) data format implemented in analog ReRAM arrays, coupled with a hybrid-domain solution framework that performs floating-point sparse matrix operations directly in the ReRAM array.

title: Late Breaking Results: Utilization of Hybrid Threshold-Voltage Flip-flops for Power Recovery
problem: Leakage power reduction in advanced technology nodes is challenging; multi-VT optimization can reduce leakage in non-critical paths, but critical-path sequential cells resist multi-VT optimization due to timing constraints.
method: Introduces hybrid-VT flip-flop cells where master and slave latches use different threshold voltages, allowing independent control of setup time and clock-to-Q delay. This decoupled control enables multi-VT optimization on critical paths without violating timing constraints. Hybrid-VT flip-flops can be applied to designs already optimized with conventional multi-VT cells.

title: Bootes: Boosting the Efficiency of Sparse Accelerators Using Spectral Clustering
problem: Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (SpGEMM) accelerators using row-wise product dataflow suffer from poor off-chip memory traffic because row reordering — the primary technique to improve data reuse — is either suboptimal, slow to compute, or fails to detect when reordering is counterproductive for certain sparsity patterns.
method: Bootes applies spectral clustering to reorder rows of the input matrix A before feeding them into a row-wise SpGEMM accelerator. A similarity matrix capturing structural properties of A's row sparsity patterns guides the clustering; similar rows are placed adjacent so that their accesses into B have high overlap, maximizing data reuse. The spectral clustering algorithm itself is optimized to reduce preprocessing time to a geometric mean of 11.61x faster than existing reordering techniques. A decision tree model trained on real-world sparse matrices predicts whether reordering will be beneficial before executing it, enabling cost-aware preprocessing that avoids overhead when reordering would increase traffic.

title: Efficient Edge Vision Transformer Accelerator with Decoupled Chunk Attention and Hybrid Computing-In-Memory
problem: Vision Transformers suffer from quadratic self-attention complexity, making them slow and resource-intensive for dense pixel-level predictions on edge devices; pyramid ViT architecture creates unbalanced workloads and poor hardware utilization.
method: Proposes decoupled chunk attention (DCA) in pipelined form to reduce off-chip memory access; combines SRAM-based computing-in-memory with RRAM nonvolatile storage; bit/element two-way-reconfigurable CIM macros adapt to varied pyramid ViT block sizes; fusion scheduling balances workload and minimizes intermediate memory.

title: Parallel Dynamic Partitioning for Datapath Combinational Equivalence Checking
problem: Datapath CEC (combinational equivalence checking) is slow and fails on complex arithmetic circuits; state-of-the-art tools cannot efficiently split and solve large datapath verification problems.
method: PDP-CEC partitions the CEC problem at critical nodes to generate independent subproblems; dynamic task scheduling ensures load balancing and prevents hard instances from blocking the overall verification.

title: HeteroSVD: Efficient SVD Accelerator on Versal ACAP with Algorithm-Hardware Co-Design
problem: Singular value decomposition (SVD) has O(n^3) complexity; real-time SVD applications (signal processing, recommendations) require acceleration. GPU and FPGA solutions don't jointly optimize latency, throughput, and power.
method: Heterogeneous FPGA accelerator on Xilinx Versal ACAP combining algorithm-hardware co-design for SVD ordering, AI Engine (AIE)-centric dataflow and placement, automatic optimization framework for performance modeling and design space exploration.

title: CMFuzz: Parallel Fuzzing of IoT Protocols by Configuration Model Identification and Scheduling
problem: Fuzzing IoT protocol implementations with fixed configurations misses bugs that emerge under alternate configurations; traditional parallel fuzzing does not account for configuration-dependent execution paths.
method: CMFuzz extracts a generalized protocol configuration model from implementations, defines relations among configuration items, and uses relation-aware allocation to distribute configurations across parallel fuzzing instances.

title: HiPER: Hierarchically-Composed Processing for Efficient Robot Learning-Based Control
problem: Learning-Based Model Predictive Control (LMPC) for robot navigation combines neural network inference with iterative MPC optimization, creating a mixed workload with rapidly varying computational patterns that neither GPUs nor simple CPU-GPU integrations can serve efficiently. The workload alternates between dense ML computation and sparse, irregular MPC solves across time steps.
method: HiPER is a 1024-PE ASIC synthesized in 16nm CMOS (16.37 mm²) built around a fractal interconnect topology that nests local systolic arrays within a hierarchical extension to handle the traffic characteristics of LMPC. A six-level pointer queue hierarchy orchestrates program composition and execution, enabling temporal and spatial mapping of workload phases at runtime. The pointer queues serve as a lightweight control mechanism that composes heterogeneous sub-programs without a complex scheduler, allowing dynamic adaptation to workload changes.

title: NVMePass: A Lightweight, High-performance and Scalable NVMe Virtualization Architecture with I/O Queues Passthrough
problem: Existing NVMe virtualization approaches either suffer severe performance degradation (Virtio software path) or require dedicated hardware with limited VM scalability (VFIO/SR-IOV hardware passthrough). No solution simultaneously achieves near-native I/O performance, zero CPU overhead, and high VM count scalability.
method: NVMePass is a software-hardware co-design that passes NVMe I/O queues directly to VMs, enabling VMs to submit commands and receive completions without hypervisor involvement. DMA and interrupt remapping are handled without hypervisor interposition. A new hardware primitive, the NVMe Resource Domain (NRD), is implemented in the NVMe controller to enforce VM-level isolation by intercepting illegal I/O requests. Logical block address ranges and I/O queues are exclusively allocated per VM for isolation without per-operation hypervisor overhead.

title: A High-Precision and Low-Cost Approximate Transform Accelerator for Video Coding
problem: The Versatile Video Coding (VVC) standard introduces multiple transform types (DCT2, DST7) requiring separate hardware implementations, leading to substantial circuit overhead and duplicated area. Efficient reuse of shared transform infrastructure while maintaining codec precision remains challenging.
method: The work exploits diagonal aggregation properties in DCT2-to-DST7 transfer matrices and applies least-squares optimization to sparsify these matrices. A lightweight matrix decomposition strategy enables a single shift-adder unit to generate product terms for multiple transform sizes (4–32 points), supporting three VVC transform types through reusable hardware.

title: ShadowBinding: Realizing Effective Microarchitectures for In-Core Secure Speculation Schemes
problem: Secure speculation schemes that mitigate Spectre-class speculative side-channel attacks (such as STT and NDA) lack rigorous RTL-level microarchitectural implementations and realistic performance/cost analysis, causing prior work to significantly underestimate their overhead. Specifically, STT's rename-stage taint computation creates an expensive single-cycle dependency chain that degrades performance on wider out-of-order cores.
method: ShadowBinding develops concrete RTL microarchitectures for two state-of-the-art secure speculation schemes—Speculative Taint Tracking (STT) and Non-Speculative Data Access (NDA)—implemented on the RISC-V Berkeley Out-of-Order Machine (BOOM). For STT, a novel variant called STT-Issue is proposed that delays taint computation from the rename stage to the issue stage, breaking the expensive single-cycle rename-stage dependency chain and improving IPC, area, and timing. RTL synthesis and cycle-accurate simulation are used to measure the combined IPC and timing impact, capturing the full performance loss including clock frequency degradation.

title: Gigaflow: Pipeline-Aware Sub-Traversal Caching for Modern SmartNICs
problem: Virtual switch (vSwitch) offloading to SmartNICs suffers from high cache miss rates and poor scalability as the flow rule space grows, because existing solutions cannot efficiently store or traverse the large and complex flow rule tables that modern cloud tenants require. This leads to bottlenecks in packet processing throughput at the NIC level.
method: Gigaflow introduces pipeline-aware sub-traversal caching, which decomposes multi-stage vSwitch packet processing pipelines into sub-traversals and caches intermediate traversal results rather than only caching complete flow lookups. By being aware of the pipeline structure, Gigaflow identifies which sub-traversal results can be safely reused across multiple packets, reducing redundant flow rule table traversals and improving NIC cache hit rates even for large flow rule spaces.

title: PairGraph: An Efficient Search-space-aware Accelerator for High-performance Concurrent Pairwise Queries
problem: Concurrent pairwise queries on graphs suffer from irregular memory access patterns and poor data sharing due to low temporal/spatial locality when multiple query paths traverse overlapping graph structures.
method: PairGraph employs a Search-space-aware Processing Model that identifies graph topology data traversed by multiple queries, identifies strong similarities in query search spaces concentrated on the topology between source-destination pairs, and reuses this shared data to minimize off-chip communications.

title: Accuracy Is Not Always We Need: Precision-Aware Bayesian Yield Optimization
problem: Integrated circuit yield optimization requires intensive simulation but existing methods uniformly allocate computational resources across all design candidates regardless of their quality potential, resulting in wasteful evaluation and slow convergence.
method: A precision-aware yield optimization framework uses a Continuous AutoRegression (CAR) model to characterize the relationship between true yield and simulation fidelity levels. A multi-fidelity acquisition strategy adaptively allocates simulation budget based on predicted design quality (Figure of Merit), balancing exploration and exploitation. The approach converges using fewer than 1,000 simulations, over 10x reduction versus high-fidelity methods.

title: Near-Memory LLM Inference Processor based on 3D DRAM-to-logic Hybrid Bonding
problem: LLM inference requires both high memory bandwidth and substantial compute resources; traditional architectures separate memory from compute, creating bandwidth bottlenecks and energy inefficiency.
method: Proposed architecture uses centralized controller and dual-IO scheme on 3D DRAM-to-logic hybrid-bonded stack. Centralized control reduces area overhead and enables reconfigurable GEMV/GEMM operations, adapting to inference phases.

title: ReMaP: Macro Placement by Recursively Prototyping and Periphery-Guided Relocating
problem: Macro placement in chip floorplanning directly impacts timing (WNS/TNS) and dataflow efficiency, but expert-quality placement is time-consuming to generate. Existing macro placers lack structured approaches to place macros near periphery while optimizing dataflow and avoiding overlaps.
method: ReMaP uses a two-phase approach: ABPlace (angle-based analytical method) arranges macros along an ellipse capturing both dataflow optimization and overlap avoidance, producing rough periphery-aligned distributions. Follow-up heuristic positions macros along chip boundaries, mimicking expert practice. Recursive refinement improves placement quality iteratively. Parameter autotuning via search optimizes tool knobs.
